199	def equivalent_task(left, right) -> dict[str, object]:
200	    """Compare two prepared, size-checked noiseless circuits."""
201	    left_qubits = left.num_qubits
202	    right_qubits = right.num_qubits
203	
204	    left_clbits, left_measurements = measurement_layout(left)
205	    right_clbits, right_measurements = measurement_layout(right)
206	
207	    if left_qubits != right_qubits:
208	        return {
209	            "schema_version": 1,
210	            "equivalent": False,
211	            "reason": "qubit_count_mismatch",
212	            "left_num_qubits": left_qubits,
213	            "right_num_qubits": right_qubits,
214	            "distance": None,
215	            "tolerance": EQUIVALENCE_TOLERANCE,
216	        }
217	
218	    distance = unitary_distance(unitary_matrix(left), unitary_matrix(right))
219	
220	    same_transform = distance <= EQUIVALENCE_TOLERANCE
221	    same_layout = left_clbits == right_clbits and left_measurements == right_measurements
222	
223	    if not same_transform:
224	        reason = "unitary_distance"
225	        equivalent = False
226	    elif not same_layout:
227	        reason = "measurement_layout_mismatch"
228	        equivalent = False
229	    else:
230	        reason = "equivalent"
231	        equivalent = True
232	
233	    return {
234	        "schema_version": 1,
235	        "equivalent": equivalent,
236	        "reason": reason,
237	        "left_num_qubits": left_qubits,
238	        "right_num_qubits": right_qubits,
239	        "distance": distance,
240	        "tolerance": EQUIVALENCE_TOLERANCE,
241	    }

259	def state_metrics_task(left, right, left_model, right_model) -> dict[str, object]:
260	    """Compare the final states of two prepared (optionally noisy) circuits."""
261	    # A noisy side evolves a full density matrix (at most MAX_NOISE_QUBITS);
262	    # a model-less side keeps the 20-qubit state-vector path.
263	    if left_model is not None and left.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
264	        raise CommandFailure(
265	            "simulation_error",
266	            f"noise simulation supports at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits, "
267	            f"left input has {left.num_qubits}",
268	            3,
269	            side="left",
270	        ) from None
271	    if right_model is not None and right.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
272	        raise CommandFailure(
273	            "simulation_error",
274	            f"noise simulation supports at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits, "
275	            f"right input has {right.num_qubits}",
276	            3,
277	            side="right",
278	        ) from None
279	
280	    noisy = left_model is not None or right_model is not None
281	
282	    left_state: list[complex] | None = None
283	    right_state: list[complex] | None = None
284	    left_rho: list[list[complex]] | None = None
285	    right_rho: list[list[complex]] | None = None
286	    if left_model is None:
287	        left_state = simulate_state_vector(left)
288	    else:
289	        left_rho = normalized_density_matrix(evolve_density_matrix(left, left_model))
290	    if right_model is None:
291	        right_state = simulate_state_vector(right)
292	    else:
293	        right_rho = normalized_density_matrix(evolve_density_matrix(right, right_model))
294	
295	    same_qubits = left.num_qubits == right.num_qubits
296	    reason = "compared" if same_qubits else "qubit_count_mismatch"
297	
298	    if not same_qubits:
299	        fidelity: float | None = None
300	    elif left_rho is None and right_rho is None:
301	        fidelity = state_fidelity(left_state, right_state)
302	    elif left_rho is not None and right_rho is not None:
303	        fidelity = density_fidelity(left_rho, right_rho)
304	    elif left_rho is not None:
305	        fidelity = pure_density_fidelity(right_state, left_rho)
306	    else:
307	        fidelity = pure_density_fidelity(left_state, right_rho)
308	
309	    left_purity = 1.0 if left_rho is None else density_purity(left_rho)
310	    right_purity = 1.0 if right_rho is None else density_purity(right_rho)
311	    left_entropy = (
312	        single_qubit_entropies(left_state, left.num_qubits)
313	        if left_rho is None
314	        else density_single_qubit_entropies(left_rho, left.num_qubits)
315	    )
316	    right_entropy = (
317	        single_qubit_entropies(right_state, right.num_qubits)
318	        if right_rho is None
319	        else density_single_qubit_entropies(right_rho, right.num_qubits)
320	    )
321	
322	    if not noisy:
323	        # No noise model on either side: keep the schema_version 1 payload
324	        # byte-for-byte identical to the historical command.
325	        return {
326	            "schema_version": 1,
327	            "left_num_qubits": left.num_qubits,
328	            "right_num_qubits": right.num_qubits,
329	            "reason": reason,
330	            "fidelity": fidelity,
331	            "left_single_qubit_entropy": left_entropy,
332	            "right_single_qubit_entropy": right_entropy,
333	        }
334	    return {
335	        "schema_version": 2,
336	        "left_num_qubits": left.num_qubits,
337	        "right_num_qubits": right.num_qubits,
338	        "reason": reason,
339	        "left_noise_model": left_model,
340	        "right_noise_model": right_model,
341	        "fidelity": fidelity,
342	        "left_purity": left_purity,
343	        "right_purity": right_purity,
344	        "left_single_qubit_entropy": left_entropy,
345	        "right_single_qubit_entropy": right_entropy,
346	    }
347	
348	
349	# ------------------------------------------------------------- batch runners
350	
351	
352	def _task_output(
353	    program,
354	    noise_model: dict[str, float] | None,
355	    shots: int,
356	    seed: int,
357	) -> tuple[dict[str, object] | None, dict[str, object] | None]:
358	    """Sample one task, converting only the simulation failure to payload."""
359	    try:
360	        return run_simulation(program, shots, seed, noise_model), None
361	    except SimulationError as exc:
362	        return None, CommandFailure("simulation_error", str(exc), 3).to_payload()
363	
364	
365	def run_batch(
366	    jobs: list[dict[str, object]],
367	    prepared: list[PreparedTask],
368	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], int]:
369	    """Execute prepared tasks in manifest order (failures embedded)."""
370	    results: list[dict[str, object]] = []
371	    succeeded = 0
372	    for job, (program, noise_model, prepare_error) in zip(jobs, prepared):
373	        output: dict[str, object] | None = None
374	        error = prepare_error
375	        if error is None:
376	            output, error = _task_output(
377	                program,
378	                noise_model,
379	                job.get("shots", 1024),
380	                job.get("seed", 0),
381	            )
382	        if error is None:
383	            succeeded += 1
384	            results.append({"id": job["id"], "status": "succeeded", "output": output})
385	        else:
386	            results.append({"id": job["id"], "status": "failed", "error": error})
387	
388	    summary: dict[str, object] = {
389	        "schema_version": BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION,
390	        "job_count": len(jobs),
391	        "succeeded": succeeded,
392	        "failed": len(jobs) - succeeded,
393	        "results": results,
394	    }
395	    return summary, 0 if succeeded == len(jobs) else 3
396	
397	
398	def run_reconcile(
399	    jobs: list[dict[str, object]],
400	    baseline: list[dict[str, object]],
401	    prepared: list[PreparedTask],
402	) -> tuple[dict[str, object], int]:
403	    """Re-run prepared tasks and diff them against the validated baseline."""
404	    entries: list[dict[str, object]] = []
405	    matched = 0
406	    for job, (program, noise_model, prepare_error), reference in zip(jobs, prepared, baseline):
407	        output: dict[str, object] | None = None
408	        error = prepare_error
409	        if error is None:
410	            output, error = _task_output(
411	                program,
412	                noise_model,
413	                job.get("shots", 1024),
414	                job.get("seed", 0),
415	            )
416	        current: dict[str, object] = (
417	            {"id": job["id"], "status": "succeeded", "output": output}
418	            if error is None
419	            else {"id": job["id"], "status": "failed", "error": error}
420	        )
421	        entry: dict[str, object] = {"id": job["id"]}
422	        if current["status"] != reference["status"]:
423	            entry["consistent"] = False
424	            entry["reason"] = "status_mismatch"
425	            entry["expected"] = reference
426	            entry["actual"] = current
427	            entries.append(entry)
428	            continue
429	
430	        if current["status"] == "succeeded":
431	            equal = json_equal(reference["output"], output)
432	            reason = "output_mismatch"
433	        else:
434	            equal = json_equal(reference["error"], error)
435	            reason = "error_mismatch"
436	
437	        if equal:
438	            entry["consistent"] = True
439	            entry["reason"] = "identical"
440	            matched += 1
441	        else:
442	            entry["consistent"] = False
443	            entry["reason"] = reason
444	            # Preserve the complete baseline and current task result.
445	            entry["expected"] = reference
446	            entry["actual"] = current
447	        entries.append(entry)
448	
449	    mismatched = len(jobs) - matched
450	    report: dict[str, object] = {
451	        "schema_version": BATCH_SCHEMA_VERSION,
452	        "job_count": len(jobs),
453	        "matched": matched,
454	        "mismatched": mismatched,
455	        "consistent": mismatched == 0,
456	        "results": entries,
457	    }
458	    return report, 0 if mismatched == 0 else 3

1	"""Input preparation for the command layer.
2	
3	This is the only layer that touches the file system and standard input.
4	Each helper reads and decodes one input, then parses and validates it,
5	returning either the prepared value or a
6	:class:`~quantum_circuit.errors.CommandFailure` whose name, message,
7	positions, ``input`` side and exit code match the historical commands
8	exactly. Helpers never write standard streams, so the validation order
9	(read errors, UTF-8 errors, parse errors, semantic errors) is expressed as
10	plain data flow and remains unit-testable.
11	
12	Paths inside batch manifests are resolved relative to *base_dir* while
13	error messages keep quoting the user-supplied path verbatim, exactly as a
14	standalone invocation would.
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import os
20	import sys
21	
22	from .errors import CommandFailure
23	from .equivalence import MAX_EQUIVALENCE_QUBITS
24	from .noise import NoiseModelError, parse_noise_model
25	from .openqasm import ParseError, Program, ValidationError, parse
26	
27	
28	def _resolve(path: str, base_dir: str | None) -> str:
29	    if base_dir is not None and not os.path.isabs(path):
30	        return os.path.normpath(os.path.join(base_dir, path))
31	    return path
32	
33	
34	def _read_bytes(path: str, base_dir: str | None) -> bytes:
35	    """Read raw bytes from *path* (resolved against *base_dir*) or stdin."""
36	    if path == "-":
37	        return sys.stdin.buffer.read()
38	    with open(_resolve(path, base_dir), "rb") as handle:
39	        return handle.read()
40	
41	
42	def _read_text(
43	    path: str,
44	    base_dir: str | None,
45	    error_name: str,
46	    noun: str,
47	    *,
48	    utf8_error: str | None = None,
49	    side: str | None = None,
50	) -> tuple[str | None, CommandFailure | None]:
51	    """Read and UTF-8 decode one document.
52	
53	    *noun* is how the input is quoted in messages (e.g. ``"source"``,
54	    ``"samples"``, ``"noise model"``). An unreadable file is *error_name*
55	    (typically ``io_error``); an invalid UTF-8 document is *utf8_error*
56	    when given (noise models use ``noise_model_error``), otherwise the
57	    same *error_name*.
58	    """
59	    try:
60	        data = _read_bytes(path, base_dir)
61	    except OSError as exc:
62	        return None, CommandFailure(
63	            error_name, f"cannot read {noun} {path!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}", 1, side=side
64	        )
65	    try:
66	        return data.decode("utf-8"), None
67	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
68	        return None, CommandFailure(
69	            utf8_error or error_name,
70	            f"{noun} {path!r} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}",
71	            2 if utf8_error is not None else 1,
72	            side=side,
73	        )
74	
75	
76	def prepare_simulation(
77	    source_arg: str,
78	    noise_model_arg: str | None,
79	    base_dir: str | None = None,
80	    register=None,
81	) -> tuple[Program | None, dict[str, float] | None, CommandFailure | None]:
82	    """Read, decode, parse and validate one simulation input.
83	
84	    Returns ``(program, noise_model, failure)``: on success *failure* is
85	    ``None`` (with *noise_model* ``None`` on the state-vector path); on
86	    failure *program* is ``None``. Reading (files, UTF-8, ``-`` for stdin,
87	    relative paths) and error semantics match ``simulate`` for both
88	    ``simulate`` and ``probabilities``. No qubit-limit or simulation error
89	    is raised here; callers apply their own limits.
90	
91	    When *base_dir* is given (the batch case), relative paths are opened
92	    relative to it while error messages keep quoting *source_arg* and
93	    *noise_model_arg* verbatim.
94	    """
95	    if noise_model_arg is not None and source_arg == "-" and noise_model_arg == "-":
96	        return (
97	            None,
98	            None,
99	            CommandFailure(
100	                "noise_model_error",
101	                "circuit source and noise model cannot both be read from standard input",
102	                2,
103	            ),
104	        )
105	
106	    try:
107	        data = _read_bytes(source_arg, base_dir)
108	    except OSError as exc:
109	        return None, None, CommandFailure(
110	            "io_error", f"cannot read source {source_arg!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}", 1
111	        )
112	    if register is not None:
113	        register(source_arg, base_dir)
114	
115	    try:
116	        source = data.decode("utf-8")
117	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
118	        return None, None, CommandFailure(
119	            "io_error", f"source {source_arg!r} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}", 1
120	        )
121	
122	    noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None
123	    if noise_model_arg is not None:
124	        # An unreadable model is io_error; invalid UTF-8 or bad content is
125	        # noise_model_error (the historical two-tier behavior).
126	        try:
127	            raw_model = _read_bytes(noise_model_arg, base_dir)
128	        except OSError as exc:
129	            return (
130	                None,
131	                None,
132	                CommandFailure(
133	                    "io_error",
134	                    f"cannot read noise model {noise_model_arg!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}",
135	                    1,
136	                ),
137	            )
138	        if register is not None:
139	            register(noise_model_arg, base_dir)
140	        try:
141	            model_text = raw_model.decode("utf-8")
142	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
143	            return (
144	                None,
145	                None,
146	                CommandFailure(
147	                    "noise_model_error",
148	                    f"noise model {noise_model_arg!r} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}",
149	                    2,
150	                ),
151	            )
152	        try:
153	            noise_model = parse_noise_model(model_text)
154	        except NoiseModelError as exc:
155	            return None, None, CommandFailure("noise_model_error", str(exc), 2)
156	
157	    try:
158	        program = parse(source)
159	    except ParseError as exc:
160	        return None, None, CommandFailure(
161	            "parse_error", exc.message, 2, line=exc.line, column=exc.column
162	        )
163	    except ValidationError as exc:
164	        return None, None, CommandFailure(
165	            "validation_error", exc.message, 2, line=exc.line, column=exc.column
166	        )
167	
168	    return program, noise_model, None
169	
170	
171	def read_document(
172	    side: str, noun: str, arg: str, register=None
173	) -> tuple[str | None, CommandFailure | None]:
174	    """Read a UTF-8 auxiliary JSON document (samples/observables) or stdin.
175	
176	    *side* is reported verbatim in the ``input`` field on every failure.
177	    """
178	    text, failure = _read_text(arg, None, "io_error", noun, side=side)
179	    if failure is None and register is not None:
180	        register(arg, None)
181	    return text, failure
182	
183	
184	def read_source(
185	    source_arg: str, register=None
186	) -> tuple[str | None, CommandFailure | None]:
187	    """Read a UTF-8 circuit source from a path or ``-`` (stdin)."""
188	    text, failure = _read_text(source_arg, None, "io_error", "source")
189	    if failure is None and register is not None:
190	        register(source_arg, None)
191	    return text, failure
192	
193	
194	def parse_program(source: str) -> tuple[Program | None, CommandFailure | None]:
195	    """Parse/validate one circuit source into a program or a failure."""
196	    try:
197	        program = parse(source)
198	    except ParseError as exc:
199	        return None, CommandFailure(
200	            "parse_error", exc.message, 2, line=exc.line, column=exc.column
201	        )
202	    except ValidationError as exc:
203	        return None, CommandFailure(
204	            "validation_error", exc.message, 2, line=exc.line, column=exc.column
205	        )
206	    return program, None
207	
208	
209	def load_program(
210	    side: str, source_arg: str, register=None
211	) -> tuple[Program | None, CommandFailure | None]:
212	    """Read, parse and validate one side of a two-circuit comparison.
213	
214	    *side* (``"left"``/``"right"``) is reported as ``input`` on every
215	    failure. Returns the parsed :class:`Program` or a failure.
216	    """
217	    source, failure = _read_text(source_arg, None, "io_error", "source", side=side)
218	    if failure is not None:
219	        return None, failure
220	    program, failure = parse_program(source)
221	    if program is None:
222	        # Tag the parse/validation failure with the comparison side.
223	        assert failure is not None
224	        return None, CommandFailure(
225	            failure.error,
226	            failure.message,
227	            failure.exit_code,
228	            side=side,
229	            line=failure.line,
230	            column=failure.column,
231	        )
232	    if register is not None:
233	        register(source_arg, None)
234	    return program, None
235	
236	
237	def load_comparison_program(
238	    side: str, source_arg: str, register=None
239	) -> tuple[Program | None, CommandFailure | None]:
240	    """Load one equivalence side, additionally enforcing the 8-qubit cap."""
241	    program, failure = load_program(side, source_arg, register)
242	    if program is None:
243	        return None, failure
244	    if program.num_qubits > MAX_EQUIVALENCE_QUBITS:
245	        return None, CommandFailure(
246	            "simulation_error",
247	            f"equivalence comparison supports at most {MAX_EQUIVALENCE_QUBITS} qubits, "
248	            f"{side} input has {program.num_qubits}",
249	            3,
250	            side=side,
251	        )
252	    return program, None
253	
254	
255	def load_metrics_noise_model(
256	    side: str, model_arg: str, register=None
257	) -> tuple[dict[str, float] | None, CommandFailure | None]:
258	    """Read and validate one side's ``state-metrics`` noise model.
259	
260	    Mirrors the ``simulate`` model handling but tags every failure with
261	    *side* (``"left"``/``"right"``).
262	    """
263	    try:
264	        raw_model = _read_bytes(model_arg, None)
265	    except OSError as exc:
266	        return None, CommandFailure(
267	            "io_error",
268	            f"cannot read noise model {model_arg!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}",
269	            1,
270	            side=side,
271	        )
272	    if register is not None:
273	        register(model_arg, None)
274	    try:
275	        model_text = raw_model.decode("utf-8")
276	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
277	        return None, CommandFailure(
278	            "noise_model_error",
279	            f"noise model {model_arg!r} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}",
280	            2,
281	            side=side,
282	        )
283	    try:
284	        return parse_noise_model(model_text), None
285	    except NoiseModelError as exc:
286	        return None, CommandFailure("noise_model_error", str(exc), 2, side=side)
287	
288	
289	def read_manifest_or_baseline(
290	    side: str, arg: str, register=None
291	) -> tuple[bytes | None, str | None, CommandFailure | None]:
292	    """Read one reconcile-style input, returning raw bytes and base dir.
293	
294	    *side* is ``"manifest"`` or ``"baseline"``. Standard input resolves
295	    *base_dir* to the current working directory; a path resolves it to
296	    the file's own directory. Bytes are UTF-8 checked but returned raw so
297	    the caller owns JSON error naming.
298	    """
299	    try:
300	        if arg == "-":
301	            raw = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
302	            base_dir = os.getcwd()
303	        else:
304	            with open(arg, "rb") as handle:
305	                raw = handle.read()
306	            base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(arg))
307	    except OSError as exc:
308	        return None, None, CommandFailure(
309	            "io_error", f"cannot read {side} {arg!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}", 1, side=side
310	        )
311	    try:
312	        raw.decode("utf-8")
313	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
314	        return None, None, CommandFailure(
315	            "io_error", f"{side} {arg!r} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}", 1, side=side
316	        )
317	    if register is not None and arg != "-":
318	        register(arg, None)
319	    return raw, base_dir, None
320	
321	
322	def read_batch_manifest(
323	    manifest_arg: str, register=None
324	) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, CommandFailure | None]:
325	    """Read and UTF-8 decode a batch-simulate manifest (path or stdin)."""
326	    if manifest_arg == "-":
327	        try:
328	            raw_manifest = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
329	        except OSError as exc:
330	            return None, None, CommandFailure(
331	                "io_error", f"cannot read manifest {manifest_arg!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}", 1
332	            )
333	        base_dir = os.getcwd()
334	    else:
335	        try:
336	            with open(manifest_arg, "rb") as handle:
337	                raw_manifest = handle.read()
338	        except OSError as exc:
339	            return None, None, CommandFailure(
340	                "io_error", f"cannot read manifest {manifest_arg!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}", 1
341	            )
342	        base_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(manifest_arg))
343	    if register is not None:
344	        register(manifest_arg, None)
345	    try:
346	        return raw_manifest.decode("utf-8"), base_dir, None
347	    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
348	        return None, None, CommandFailure(
349	            "io_error", f"manifest {manifest_arg!r} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}", 1
350	        )

1	"""CLI-independent simulation application core.
2	
3	Both the command line (``simulate``, ``probabilities``, ``expectation``
4	and ``verify-samples``) and the Python DSL (:class:`~quantum_circuit.circuit.Circuit`)
5	prepare and validate their own inputs, then delegate here for the actual
6	work: state evolution, measurement probability aggregation, deterministic
7	sampling and canonical success-payload assembly.
8	
9	This module never imports :mod:`quantum_circuit.cli` and performs no file,
10	standard input, environment or standard stream access. It receives only a
11	validated :class:`~quantum_circuit.openqasm.Program` together with already
12	validated sampling parameters and a canonical noise model (as produced by
13	:func:`quantum_circuit.noise.validate_noise_model` /
14	:func:`quantum_circuit.noise.parse_noise_model`); failures intrinsic to a
15	simulation are reported as :class:`SimulationError`.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import math
21	
22	from .metrics import normalized_density_matrix
23	from .noise import MAX_NOISE_QUBITS, evolve_density_matrix, simulate_density_matrix
24	from .observables import (
25	    density_matrix_expectation,
26	    snap_expectation,
27	    state_vector_expectation,
28	)
29	from .openqasm import Program
30	from .simulator import (
31	    measurement_probabilities,
32	    sample_counts,
33	    sample_counts_from_probabilities,
34	    simulate_state_vector,
35	)
36	
37	# Probabilities are reported in full; entries this close to 0 are omitted
38	# and entries this close to 1 are reported as exactly 1. Reported values
39	# sum to within 1e-12 of 1.
40	PROBABILITY_ZERO_TOLERANCE = 1e-15
41	PROBABILITY_ONE_TOLERANCE = 1e-15
42	
43	
44	class SimulationError(Exception):
45	    """The prepared circuit cannot be simulated (``simulation_error``).
46	
47	    The only current case is a noisy circuit beyond the density-matrix
48	    qubit limit; command-line callers map it to exit code 3.
49	    """
50	
51	
52	def noisy_qubit_limit_error(num_qubits: int) -> SimulationError:
53	    return SimulationError(
54	        f"noise simulation supports at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits, "
55	        f"got {num_qubits}"
56	    )
57	
58	
59	def snap_probability(value: float) -> float | None:
60	    """Snap one probability for deterministic output.
61	
62	    Returns ``None`` when the entry is omitted (magnitude at most
63	    ``1e-15``), ``1.0`` when it is within ``1e-15`` of 1, and otherwise a
64	    finite ``float`` clamped to ``(0, 1)`` so simulation round-off can
65	    never produce an out-of-range value.
66	    """
67	    if abs(value) <= PROBABILITY_ZERO_TOLERANCE:
68	        return None
69	    if abs(1.0 - value) <= PROBABILITY_ONE_TOLERANCE:
70	        return 1.0
71	    return min(1.0, max(0.0, float(value)))
72	
73	
74	def evolve_basis_probabilities(
75	    program: Program, noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None
76	) -> list[float]:
77	    """Evolve *program* and return per-basis-state measurement probabilities.
78	
79	    Without a noise model the final state vector is evolved (the parser
80	    caps registers at the 20-qubit limit) and amplitudes are squared; with
81	    one the density matrix is evolved (at most :data:`~quantum_circuit.noise.MAX_NOISE_QUBITS`
82	    qubits) and its diagonal returned. Raises :class:`SimulationError` when
83	    a noisy circuit exceeds the density-matrix limit.
84	    """
85	    if noise_model is None:
86	        state = simulate_state_vector(program)
87	        return [abs(amplitude) ** 2 for amplitude in state]
88	    if program.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
89	        raise noisy_qubit_limit_error(program.num_qubits)
90	    return simulate_density_matrix(program, noise_model)
91	
92	
93	def probability_payload(
94	    program: Program,
95	    basis_probabilities: list[float],
96	    noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None,
97	) -> dict[str, object]:
98	    """Build the deterministic ``probabilities`` success payload.
99	
100	    The aggregated classical distribution is renormalized by its total
101	    first, mirroring the normalization the sampling path applies to basis
102	    probabilities, so simulation round-off (notably density-matrix drift)
103	    cannot move the reported sum away from 1.
104	    """
105	    aggregated = measurement_probabilities(program, basis_probabilities)
106	    total = math.fsum(aggregated.values())

"""CLI-independent simulation application core.

Both the command line (``simulate``, ``probabilities``, ``expectation``
and ``verify-samples``) and the Python DSL (:class:`~quantum_circuit.circuit.Circuit`)
prepare and validate their own inputs, then delegate here for the actual
work: state evolution, measurement probability aggregation, deterministic
sampling and canonical success-payload assembly.

This module never imports :mod:`quantum_circuit.cli` and performs no file,
standard input, environment or standard stream access. It receives only a
validated :class:`~quantum_circuit.openqasm.Program` together with already
validated sampling parameters and a canonical noise model (as produced by
:func:`quantum_circuit.noise.validate_noise_model` /
:func:`quantum_circuit.noise.parse_noise_model`); failures intrinsic to a
simulation are reported as :class:`SimulationError`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

from .metrics import normalized_density_matrix
from .noise import MAX_NOISE_QUBITS, evolve_density_matrix, simulate_density_matrix
from .observables import (
    density_matrix_expectation,
    snap_expectation,
    state_vector_expectation,
)
from .openqasm import Program
from .simulator import (
    measurement_probabilities,
    sample_counts,
    sample_counts_from_probabilities,
    simulate_state_vector,
)

# Probabilities are reported in full; entries this close to 0 are omitted
# and entries this close to 1 are reported as exactly 1. Reported values
# sum to within 1e-12 of 1.
PROBABILITY_ZERO_TOLERANCE = 1e-15
PROBABILITY_ONE_TOLERANCE = 1e-15


class SimulationError(Exception):
    """The prepared circuit cannot be simulated (``simulation_error``).

    The only current case is a noisy circuit beyond the density-matrix
    qubit limit; command-line callers map it to exit code 3.
    """


def noisy_qubit_limit_error(num_qubits: int) -> SimulationError:
    return SimulationError(
        f"noise simulation supports at most {MAX_NOISE_QUBITS} qubits, "
        f"got {num_qubits}"
    )


def snap_probability(value: float) -> float | None:
    """Snap one probability for deterministic output.

    Returns ``None`` when the entry is omitted (magnitude at most
    ``1e-15``), ``1.0`` when it is within ``1e-15`` of 1, and otherwise a
    finite ``float`` clamped to ``(0, 1)`` so simulation round-off can
    never produce an out-of-range value.
    """
    if abs(value) <= PROBABILITY_ZERO_TOLERANCE:
        return None
    if abs(1.0 - value) <= PROBABILITY_ONE_TOLERANCE:
        return 1.0
    return min(1.0, max(0.0, float(value)))


def evolve_basis_probabilities(
    program: Program, noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None
) -> list[float]:
    """Evolve *program* and return per-basis-state measurement probabilities.

    Without a noise model the final state vector is evolved (the parser
    caps registers at the 20-qubit limit) and amplitudes are squared; with
    one the density matrix is evolved (at most :data:`~quantum_circuit.noise.MAX_NOISE_QUBITS`
    qubits) and its diagonal returned. Raises :class:`SimulationError` when
    a noisy circuit exceeds the density-matrix limit.
    """
    if noise_model is None:
        state = simulate_state_vector(program)
        return [abs(amplitude) ** 2 for amplitude in state]
    if program.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
        raise noisy_qubit_limit_error(program.num_qubits)
    return simulate_density_matrix(program, noise_model)


def probability_payload(
    program: Program,
    basis_probabilities: list[float],
    noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Build the deterministic ``probabilities`` success payload.

    The aggregated classical distribution is renormalized by its total
    first, mirroring the normalization the sampling path applies to basis
    probabilities, so simulation round-off (notably density-matrix drift)
    cannot move the reported sum away from 1.
    """
    aggregated = measurement_probabilities(program, basis_probabilities)
    total = math.fsum(aggregated.values())
    probabilities: dict[str, float] = {}
    for key, value in aggregated.items():
        normalized = value / total if total else value
        snapped = snap_probability(normalized)
        if snapped is not None:
            probabilities[key] = snapped

    if noise_model is None:
        return {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
            "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
            "probabilities": probabilities,
        }
    return {
        "schema_version": 2,
        "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
        "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
        "noise_model": noise_model,
        "probabilities": probabilities,
    }


def run_probabilities(
    program: Program, noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Evolve *program* and assemble its ``probabilities`` payload."""
    basis_probabilities = evolve_basis_probabilities(program, noise_model)
    return probability_payload(program, basis_probabilities, noise_model)


def run_expectation(
    program: Program,
    noise_model: dict[str, float] | None,
    observables: list[tuple[str, list[tuple[int, str]]]],
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Evaluate every observable against the final (pre-measurement) state.

    *observables* is a validated batch of ``(id, operators)`` pairs in
    input order, each operator a ``(qubit, pauli)`` tuple. Without a noise
    model the state vector is evolved and ``<psi|P|psi>`` reported; with
    one the normalized density matrix is evolved (at most
    :data:`~quantum_circuit.noise.MAX_NOISE_QUBITS` qubits) and
    ``Tr(rho P)`` reported. Raises :class:`SimulationError` when a noisy
    circuit exceeds the density-matrix qubit limit.
    """
    if noise_model is None:
        # The parser already caps the register at the 20-qubit
        # state-vector limit.
        state = simulate_state_vector(program)
        results = [
            {
                "id": observable_id,
                "expectation": snap_expectation(state_vector_expectation(state, operators)),
            }
            for observable_id, operators in observables
        ]
        return {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
            "noise_model": None,
            "results": results,
        }

    if program.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
        raise noisy_qubit_limit_error(program.num_qubits)
    rho = normalized_density_matrix(evolve_density_matrix(program, noise_model))
    results = [
        {
            "id": observable_id,
            "expectation": snap_expectation(density_matrix_expectation(rho, operators)),
        }
        for observable_id, operators in observables
    ]
    return {
        "schema_version": 1,
        "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
        "noise_model": noise_model,
        "results": results,
    }


def run_simulation(
    program: Program,
    shots: int,
    seed: int,
    noise_model: dict[str, float] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Evolve a prepared circuit and sample it (the ``simulate`` payload).

    Sampling draws from a fresh RNG seeded by *seed*, so equal arguments
    produce equal results and no random state is shared between calls.
    Raises :class:`SimulationError` when a noisy circuit exceeds the
    density-matrix qubit limit.
    """
    if noise_model is None:
        state = simulate_state_vector(program)
        counts = sample_counts(program, state, shots, seed)
        return {
            "schema_version": 1,
            "shots": shots,
            "seed": seed,
            "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
            "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
            "counts": counts,
        }
    if program.num_qubits > MAX_NOISE_QUBITS:
        raise noisy_qubit_limit_error(program.num_qubits)
    probabilities = simulate_density_matrix(program, noise_model)
    counts = sample_counts_from_probabilities(program, probabilities, shots, seed)
    return {
        "schema_version": 2,
        "shots": shots,
        "seed": seed,
        "num_qubits": program.num_qubits,
        "num_clbits": program.num_clbits,
        "noise_model": noise_model,
        "counts": counts,
    }

1	"""Python DSL for building circuits over the OpenQASM 2.0 subset.
2	
3	A :class:`Circuit` is created with a quantum and a classical register size
4	and extended by chaining gate and measurement methods, mirroring the
5	statements of the supported OpenQASM subset one to one::
6	
7	    circuit = Circuit(2, 2).h(0).cx(0, 1).measure(0, 0).measure(1, 1)
8	
9	Operations keep their insertion order and every chaining method returns the
10	same circuit object. The circuit renders to (:meth:`Circuit.to_qasm`) and
11	parses from (:meth:`Circuit.from_qasm`) the OpenQASM 2.0 subset text the
12	command line accepts, and simulates through the exact code paths of the
13	``simulate``, ``probabilities`` and ``expectation`` commands
14	(:meth:`Circuit.sample`, :meth:`Circuit.probabilities`,
15	:meth:`Circuit.expectation`), so the returned dictionaries match the
16	commands' JSON objects field by field.
17	
18	Validation mirrors the parser's semantic rules: type mismatches raise
19	:class:`TypeError`, while out-of-range indices, non-finite angles and
20	semantic conflicts (control equal to target, repeated measurement, a gate
21	after a measurement) raise :class:`ValueError`. A rejected operation never
22	changes the circuit.
23	"""
24	
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	import math
28	from collections.abc import Mapping
29	
30	from .core import SimulationError, run_expectation, run_probabilities, run_simulation
31	from .gates import (
32	    Operation,
33	    gate_operation,
34	    gate_qasm,
35	    measurement_operation,
36	)
37	from .noise import validate_noise_model
38	from .observables import MAX_OBSERVABLES
39	from .openqasm import Program, parse
40	
41	# Register sizes accepted by the DSL match the parser's limit.
42	_MIN_REGISTER_SIZE = 1
43	_MAX_REGISTER_SIZE = 20
44	
45	_DEFAULT_SHOTS = 1024
46	_DEFAULT_SEED = 0
47	
48	
49	def _check_register_size(name: str, value: object) -> int:
50	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
51	        raise TypeError(
52	            f"{name} must be an integer, got {type(value).__name__}"
53	        )
54	    if not _MIN_REGISTER_SIZE <= value <= _MAX_REGISTER_SIZE:
55	        raise ValueError(
56	            f"{name} must be between {_MIN_REGISTER_SIZE} and {_MAX_REGISTER_SIZE}, got {value}"
57	        )
58	    return value
59	
60	
61	def _check_index(register: str, value: object, size: int) -> int:
62	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
63	        raise TypeError(
64	            f"{register} index must be an integer, got {type(value).__name__}"
65	        )
66	    if not 0 <= value < size:
67	        raise ValueError(
68	            f"{register} index {value} out of range for register of size {size}"
69	        )
70	    return value
71	
72	
73	def _check_angle(value: object) -> float:
74	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
75	        raise TypeError(
76	            f"angle must be an integer or float, got {type(value).__name__}"
77	        )
78	    angle = float(value)
79	    if not math.isfinite(angle):
80	        raise ValueError("angle must be a finite number")
81	    return angle
82	
83	
84	def _operation_line(op: Operation) -> str:
85	    """Render one operation as an OpenQASM statement (register names q/c)."""
86	    if op.kind == "measure":
87	        return f"measure q[{op.targets[0]}] -> c[{op.targets[1]}];"
88	    return gate_qasm(op.kind, op.targets, op.params[0] if op.params else None)
89	
90	
91	_OBSERVABLE_KEYS = ("id", "operators")
92	_OPERATOR_KEYS = ("qubit", "pauli")
93	_PAULIS = ("X", "Y", "Z")
94	
95	
96	def _check_observable_operators(
97	    operators: object, where: str, num_qubits: int
98	) -> list[tuple[int, str]]:
99	    if isinstance(operators, bool) or not isinstance(operators, (list, tuple)):
100	        raise TypeError(
101	            f"{where} 'operators' must be a list or tuple, "
102	            f"got {type(operators).__name__}"
103	        )
104	    parsed: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
105	    seen_qubits: set[int] = set()
106	    for op_index, operator in enumerate(operators):
107	        op_where = f"{where}.operators[{op_index}]"
108	        if not isinstance(operator, Mapping):
109	            raise TypeError(
110	                f"{op_where} must be a mapping, got {type(operator).__name__}"
111	            )
112	        for key in operator:
113	            if key not in _OPERATOR_KEYS:
114	                raise ValueError(f"{op_where} has unknown field {key!r}")
115	
116	        if "qubit" not in operator:
117	            raise ValueError(f"{op_where} is missing required field 'qubit'")
118	        qubit = operator["qubit"]
119	        if isinstance(qubit, bool) or not isinstance(qubit, int):
120	            raise TypeError(
121	                f"{op_where} 'qubit' must be an integer, "
122	                f"got {type(qubit).__name__}"
123	            )
124	        if not 0 <= qubit < num_qubits:
125	            raise ValueError(
126	                f"{op_where} 'qubit' {qubit} out of range for register of "
127	                f"size {num_qubits}"
128	            )
129	        if qubit in seen_qubits:
130	            raise ValueError(f"{op_where} repeats qubit {qubit} within {where}")
131	        seen_qubits.add(qubit)
132	
133	        if "pauli" not in operator:
134	            raise ValueError(f"{op_where} is missing required field 'pauli'")
135	        pauli = operator["pauli"]
136	        if not isinstance(pauli, str):
137	            raise TypeError(
138	                f"{op_where} 'pauli' must be a string, got {type(pauli).__name__}"
139	            )
140	        if pauli not in _PAULIS:
141	            raise ValueError(
142	                f"{op_where} 'pauli' must be one of 'X', 'Y', 'Z', got {pauli!r}"
143	            )
144	
145	        parsed.append((qubit, pauli))
146	    return parsed
147	
148	
149	def _check_observables(
150	    observables: object, num_qubits: int
151	) -> list[tuple[str, list[tuple[int, str]]]]:
152	    """Validate one observables batch, returning ``(id, operators)`` pairs.
153	
154	    Type mismatches raise :class:`TypeError`; size, field, identifier,
155	    qubit and Pauli violations raise :class:`ValueError`. The whole batch
156	    is checked before any state evolution happens.
157	    """
158	    if isinstance(observables, bool) or not isinstance(observables, (list, tuple)):
159	        raise TypeError(
160	            f"observables must be a list or tuple, got {type(observables).__name__}"
161	        )
162	    if not 1 <= len(observables) <= MAX_OBSERVABLES:
163	        raise ValueError(
164	            f"observables must contain between 1 and {MAX_OBSERVABLES} entries, "
165	            f"got {len(observables)}"
166	        )
167	
168	    parsed: list[tuple[str, list[tuple[int, str]]]] = []
169	    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
170	    for index, item in enumerate(observables):
171	        where = f"observables[{index}]"
172	        if not isinstance(item, Mapping):
173	            raise TypeError(f"{where} must be a mapping, got {type(item).__name__}")
174	        for key in item:
175	            if key not in _OBSERVABLE_KEYS:
176	                raise ValueError(f"{where} has unknown field {key!r}")
177	
178	        if "id" not in item:
179	            raise ValueError(f"{where} is missing required field 'id'")
180	        observable_id = item["id"]
181	        if not isinstance(observable_id, str):
182	            raise TypeError(
183	                f"{where} 'id' must be a string, got {type(observable_id).__name__}"
184	            )
185	        if not observable_id:
186	            raise ValueError(f"{where} 'id' must be a non-empty string")
187	        if observable_id in seen_ids:
188	            raise ValueError(f"duplicate observable id {observable_id!r}")
189	        seen_ids.add(observable_id)
190	
191	        if "operators" not in item:
192	            raise ValueError(f"{where} is missing required field 'operators'")
193	        parsed.append(
194	            (
195	                observable_id,
196	                _check_observable_operators(item["operators"], where, num_qubits),
197	            )
198	        )
199	    return parsed
200	
201	
202	class Circuit:
203	    """A quantum circuit over the supported OpenQASM 2.0 subset.
204	
205	    Created with the quantum and classical register sizes (integers from 1
206	    to 20, booleans rejected) and extended through the chaining gate and
207	    measurement methods, which return the circuit itself.
208	    """
209	
210	    def __init__(self, num_qubits: int, num_clbits: int):
211	        self._num_qubits = _check_register_size("num_qubits", num_qubits)
212	        self._num_clbits = _check_register_size("num_clbits", num_clbits)
213	        self._operations: list[Operation] = []
214	        self._measured_qubits: set[int] = set()
215	        self._measured_clbits: set[int] = set()
216	        self._measurement_started = False
217	
218	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ properties
219	
220	    @property
221	    def num_qubits(self) -> int:
222	        return self._num_qubits
223	
224	    @property
225	    def num_clbits(self) -> int:
226	        return self._num_clbits
227	
228	    @property
229	    def operations(self) -> tuple[Operation, ...]:
230	        """The appended operations, in insertion order."""
231	        return tuple(self._operations)
232	
233	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
234	        return (
235	            f"Circuit(num_qubits={self._num_qubits}, num_clbits={self._num_clbits}, "
236	            f"operations={len(self._operations)})"
237	        )
238	
239	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ gates
240	
241	    def _qubit_index(self, value: object) -> int:
242	        return _check_index("qubit", value, self._num_qubits)
243	
244	    def _clbit_index(self, value: object) -> int:
245	        return _check_index("clbit", value, self._num_clbits)
246	
247	    def _check_gate_allowed(self, kind: str) -> None:
248	        if self._measurement_started:
249	            raise ValueError(f"quantum gate {kind!r} cannot be added after a measurement")
250	
251	    def _append_gate(self, op: Operation) -> Circuit:
252	        # All validation has already happened in the calling method, so a
253	        # rejected operation never reaches this point and never mutates the
254	        # circuit.
255	        self._operations.append(op)
256	        return self
257	
258	    def _fixed_single_gate(self, name: str, qubit: object) -> Circuit:
259	        target = self._qubit_index(qubit)
260	        self._check_gate_allowed(name)
261	        return self._append_gate(gate_operation(name, (target,)))
262	
263	    def _controlled_gate(self, name: str, control: object, target: object) -> Circuit:
264	        ctrl = self._qubit_index(control)
265	        tgt = self._qubit_index(target)
266	        if ctrl == tgt:
267	            raise ValueError(f"{name} control and target must be different qubits")
268	        self._check_gate_allowed(name)
269	        return self._append_gate(gate_operation(name, (ctrl, tgt)))
270

272	        a = self._qubit_index(first)

366	    def measure(self, qubit: int, clbit: int) -> Circuit:
367	        """Append ``measure qubit -> clbit``.
368	
369	        Each qubit and each clbit may take part in at most one measurement,
370	        and no quantum gate may be added once measurement has started.
371	        """
372	        q = self._qubit_index(qubit)
373	        c = self._clbit_index(clbit)
374	        if q in self._measured_qubits:
375	            raise ValueError(f"qubit {q} is measured more than once")
376	        if c in self._measured_clbits:
377	            raise ValueError(f"clbit {c} is the target of more than one measurement")
378	        self._measured_qubits.add(q)
379	        self._measured_clbits.add(c)
380	        self._measurement_started = True
381	        self._operations.append(measurement_operation(q, c))
382	        return self

384	    # --------------------------------------------------------------- OpenQASM

386	    def to_qasm(self) -> str:
387	        """Render the circuit as OpenQASM 2.0 subset text.
388	
389	        Uses the fixed register names ``q`` and ``c``, emits the operations
390	        in insertion order with the same statement semantics as the parser,
391	        and ends with a trailing newline. Angles use the shortest decimal
392	        representation that round-trips to the same float (negative zero is
393	        written as ``0``).
394	        """
395	        lines = [
396	            "OPENQASM 2.0;",
397	            'include "qelib1.inc";',
398	            f"qreg q[{self._num_qubits}];",
399	            f"creg c[{self._num_clbits}];",
400	        ]
401	        lines.extend(_operation_line(op) for op in self._operations)
402	        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
403	
404	    @classmethod
405	    def from_qasm(cls, source: str) -> Circuit:
406	        """Build a circuit from OpenQASM 2.0 subset text.
407	
408	        Parsing and validation are exactly those of the command line:
409	        :class:`~quantum_circuit.openqasm.ParseError` and
410	        :class:`~quantum_circuit.openqasm.ValidationError` propagate with
411	        their 1-based line/column positions intact.
412	        """
413	        if not isinstance(source, str):
414	            raise TypeError(f"source must be a string, got {type(source).__name__}")
415	        program = parse(source)
416	        circuit = cls(program.num_qubits, program.num_clbits)
417	        for op in program.operations:
418	            # The program is fully validated, so these invariants hold.
419	            if op.kind == "measure":
420	                circuit._measured_qubits.add(op.targets[0])
421	                circuit._measured_clbits.add(op.targets[1])
422	                circuit._measurement_started = True
423	            circuit._operations.append(op)
424	        return circuit
425	
426	    # -------------------------------------------------------------- simulation
427	
428	    def _to_program(self) -> Program:
429	        return Program(self._num_qubits, self._num_clbits, tuple(self._operations))

431	    @staticmethod
432	    def _prepare_noise_model(noise_model: object) -> dict[str, float] | None:
433	        if noise_model is None:
434	            return None
435	        return validate_noise_model(noise_model)

437	    def sample(self, shots: int = _DEFAULT_SHOTS, seed: int = _DEFAULT_SEED, noise_model=None) -> dict:
438	        """Sample the circuit, returning the ``simulate`` payload as a dict.
439	
440	        The result equals the JSON object the ``simulate`` command produces
441	        for :meth:`to_qasm` with the same *shots*, *seed* and noise model
442	        (defaults 1024 and 0). *noise_model* is a mapping with the four
443	        optional channels; invalid models raise
444	        :class:`~quantum_circuit.noise.NoiseModelError`. Each call samples
445	        from a fresh RNG seeded by *seed*, so repeated calls with equal
446	        arguments return equal results and no random state is shared. The
447	        circuit itself is never modified.
448	        """
449	        if isinstance(shots, bool) or not isinstance(shots, int):
450	            raise TypeError(f"shots must be an integer, got {type(shots).__name__}")
451	        if shots <= 0:
452	            raise ValueError(f"shots must be a positive integer, got {shots}")
453	        if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
454	            raise TypeError(f"seed must be an integer, got {type(seed).__name__}")
455	        model = self._prepare_noise_model(noise_model)
456	        program = self._to_program()
457	        try:
458	            return run_simulation(program, shots, seed, model)
459	        except SimulationError as exc:
460	            # The DSL reports the noisy size limit as a ValueError, matching
461	            # its other value-range errors rather than the CLI's exit code 3.
462	            raise ValueError(str(exc)) from None
463	
464	    def probabilities(self, noise_model=None) -> dict:
465	        """Exact final-state measurement probabilities, as a dict.
466	
467	        The result equals the JSON object the ``probabilities`` command
468	        produces for :meth:`to_qasm` with the same noise model. The circuit
469	        itself is never modified.
470	        """
471	        model = self._prepare_noise_model(noise_model)
472	        program = self._to_program()
473	        try:
474	            return run_probabilities(program, model)
475	        except SimulationError as exc:
476	            raise ValueError(str(exc)) from None

478	    def expectation(self, observables, noise_model=None) -> dict:
479	        """Pauli-product expectation values of the final pre-measurement state.
480	
481	        *observables* is a list or tuple of 1 to 100 mappings, each with an
482	        ``id`` (a non-empty string, unique within the batch) and
483	        ``operators`` (a list or tuple of mappings with a ``qubit`` — a
484	        non-boolean integer inside the quantum register, not repeated
485	        within one entry — and a ``pauli`` of ``"X"``, ``"Y"`` or
486	        ``"Z"``). An empty ``operators`` sequence is the global identity.
487	        Type mismatches raise :class:`TypeError`; size, field, identifier,
488	        qubit and Pauli violations raise :class:`ValueError`, and the whole
489	        batch is validated before any state evolution happens.
490	
491	        The result equals the JSON object the ``expectation`` command
492	        produces for :meth:`to_qasm` with the equivalent observables
493	        document and the same noise model, keeping the input order:
494	        ``schema_version``, ``num_qubits``, ``noise_model`` (``None``
495	        without a model) and ``results``, each result carrying the original
496	        ``id`` and its ``expectation`` in ``[-1, 1]``. Measurement mappings
497	        and the classical register width do not take part. Invalid noise
498	        models raise :class:`~quantum_circuit.noise.NoiseModelError`; a
499	        noisy circuit beyond the density-matrix qubit limit raises
500	        :class:`ValueError`. Repeated calls with equal arguments return
501	        equal results, and neither the circuit nor *observables* is
502	        modified.
503	        """
504	        parsed = _check_observables(observables, self._num_qubits)
505	        model = self._prepare_noise_model(noise_model)
506	        program = self._to_program()
507	        try:
508	            return run_expectation(program, model, parsed)
509	        except SimulationError as exc:

16	_SQRT1_2 = 2.0**-0.5
17	
18	
19	def _hadamard(state: list[complex], qubit: int, num_qubits: int) -> None:
20	    bit = 1 << qubit
21	    step = bit << 1
22	    for base in range(0, 1 << num_qubits, step):
23	        for low in range(base, base + bit):
24	            high = low | bit
25	            a = state[low]
26	            b = state[high]
27	            state[low] = (a + b) * _SQRT1_2
28	            state[high] = (a - b) * _SQRT1_2
29	
30	
31	def _pauli_x(state: list[complex], qubit: int, num_qubits: int) -> None:
32	    bit = 1 << qubit
33	    step = bit << 1
34	    for base in range(0, 1 << num_qubits, step):
35	        for low in range(base, base + bit):
36	            high = low | bit
37	            state[low], state[high] = state[high], state[low]
38	
39	
40	def _pauli_y(state: list[complex], qubit: int, num_qubits: int) -> None:
41	    bit = 1 << qubit
42	    step = bit << 1
43	    for base in range(0, 1 << num_qubits, step):
44	        for low in range(base, base + bit):
45	            high = low | bit
46	            a = state[low]
47	            b = state[high]
48	            state[low] = -1j * b
49	            state[high] = 1j * a

52	# Phase gates diag(1, phase): z, s/sdg (diag(1, +-i)) and t/tdg
53	# (phase exp(+-i*pi/4)). The factors come from the single gate registry so
54	# the state-vector path cannot diverge from the density/unitary matrices.
55	_PHASE_GATES = PHASE_FACTORS

57	
58	def _phase(state: list[complex], qubit: int, num_qubits: int, factor: complex) -> None:
59	    bit = 1 << qubit
60	    for index in range(1 << num_qubits):
61	        if index & bit:
62	            state[index] = factor * state[index]
63	
64	
65	def _swap(state: list[complex], first: int, second: int, num_qubits: int) -> None:
66	    first_bit = 1 << first
67	    second_bit = 1 << second
68	    for index in range(1 << num_qubits):
69	        if (index & first_bit) and not (index & second_bit):
70	            other = (index ^ first_bit) | second_bit
71	            state[index], state[other] = state[other], state[index]
72	
73	
74	def _controlled_x(state: list[complex], control: int, target: int, num_qubits: int) -> None:
75	    cbit = 1 << control
76	    tbit = 1 << target
77	    for index in range(1 << num_qubits):
78	        if (index & cbit) and not (index & tbit):
79	            other = index | tbit
80	            if index < other:
81	                state[index], state[other] = state[other], state[index]
82	
83	
84	def _controlled_single(
85	    state: list[complex],
86	    control: int,
87	    target: int,
88	    num_qubits: int,
89	    matrix: tuple[complex, complex, complex, complex],
90	) -> None:
91	    """Apply a single-qubit matrix to *target* where the *control* bit is 1."""
92	    g00, g01, g10, g11 = matrix
93	    cbit = 1 << control
94	    tbit = 1 << target
95	    step = tbit << 1
96	    for base in range(0, 1 << num_qubits, step):
97	        for low in range(base, base + tbit):
98	            if not (low & cbit):
99	                continue
100	            high = low | tbit
101	            a = state[low]
102	            b = state[high]
103	            state[low] = g00 * a + g01 * b
104	            state[high] = g10 * a + g11 * b
105

107	def _rx(state: list[complex], qubit: int, num_qubits: int, theta: float) -> None:
108	    c = math.cos(theta / 2)
109	    s = math.sin(theta / 2)
110	    bit = 1 << qubit
111	    step = bit << 1
112	    for base in range(0, 1 << num_qubits, step):
113	        for low in range(base, base + bit):
114	            high = low | bit
115	            a = state[low]
116	            b = state[high]
117	            state[low] = c * a - 1j * s * b
118	            state[high] = -1j * s * a + c * b
119	
120	
121	def _ry(state: list[complex], qubit: int, num_qubits: int, theta: float) -> None:
122	    c = math.cos(theta / 2)
123	    s = math.sin(theta / 2)
124	    bit = 1 << qubit
125	    step = bit << 1
126	    for base in range(0, 1 << num_qubits, step):
127	        for low in range(base, base + bit):
128	            high = low | bit
129	            a = state[low]
130	            b = state[high]
131	            state[low] = c * a - s * b
132	            state[high] = s * a + c * b
133	
134	
135	def _rz(state: list[complex], qubit: int, num_qubits: int, theta: float) -> None:
136	    lo_factor = cmath.exp(-0.5j * theta)
137	    hi_factor = cmath.exp(0.5j * theta)
138	    bit = 1 << qubit
139	    for index in range(1 << num_qubits):
140	        if index & bit:
141	            state[index] = hi_factor * state[index]
142	        else:
143	            state[index] = lo_factor * state[index]

146	def _apply_gate(state: list[complex], op: Operation, num_qubits: int) -> None:
147	    """Apply one (non-measurement) *op* to *state* in place.
148	
149	    The dispatch uses the gate's registered style and the single shared
150	    matrix expression in :mod:`quantum_circuit.gates`; only the numeric
151	    state-vector kernels below are local to this module.
152	    """
153	    kind = op.kind
154	    if kind == "x":
155	        _pauli_x(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits)
156	    elif kind == "h":
157	        _hadamard(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits)
158	    elif kind == "y":
159	        _pauli_y(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits)
160	    elif kind in _PHASE_GATES:
161	        _phase(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits, _PHASE_GATES[kind])
162	    elif kind == "swap":
163	        _swap(state, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], num_qubits)
164	    elif kind == "cx":
165	        _controlled_x(state, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], num_qubits)
166	    elif kind == "cz":
167	        _controlled_single(
168	            state, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], num_qubits, op.spec.target_unitary()
169	        )
170	    elif kind in ("rx", "ry", "rz"):
171	        axis = op.spec.axis
172	        if axis == "x":
173	            _rx(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits, op.params[0])
174	        elif axis == "y":
175	            _ry(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits, op.params[0])
176	        else:
177	            _rz(state, op.targets[0], num_qubits, op.params[0])
178	    else:
179	        # Controlled angle rotations crx/cry/crz: the target embedding is
180	        # the one matrix definition shared with the density path.
181	        matrix = rotation_matrix(op.spec.axis, op.params[0])
182	        _controlled_single(state, op.targets[0], op.targets[1], num_qubits, matrix)

185	def simulate_state_vector(program: Program) -> list[complex]:
186	    """Return the final state vector after applying all quantum gates.
187	
188	    Basis-state integer ``k`` stores qubit ``i`` in bit ``i`` (q[0] is the
189	    least significant bit). Measurements do not collapse the state: the spec
190	    guarantees every measurement comes after every gate and each qubit is
191	    measured at most once, so non-destructive sampling of the final state is
192	    equivalent.
193	    """
194	    n = program.num_qubits
195	    state = [0j] * (1 << n)
196	    state[0] = 1 + 0j
197	
198	    for op in program.operations:
199	        if op.kind == "measure":
200	            # Measurements affect only the sampled classical outcomes.
201	            continue
202	        _apply_gate(state, op, n)
203	    return state
204

206	def unitary_matrix(program: Program) -> list[list[complex]]:
207	    """Return the full unitary U induced by the gates (pre-measurement).
208	
209	    The matrix acts on basis vectors with qubit ``i`` in bit ``i`` (q[0] is
210	    the least significant bit), matching :func:`simulate_state_vector`.
211	    Measurement operations are ignored. Columns are evolved independently by
212	    applying each gate in source order, so for a circuit with gates G1..Gk the
213	    result is U = Gk @ ... @ G1.
214	    """
215	    n = program.num_qubits
216	    dim = 1 << n
217	    gate_ops = [op for op in program.operations if op.kind != "measure"]
218	
219	    columns: list[list[complex]] = []
220	    for start in range(dim):
221	        state = [0j] * dim
222	        state[start] = 1 + 0j
223	        for op in gate_ops:
224	            _apply_gate(state, op, n)
225	        columns.append(state)
226	
227	    # Transpose columns-of-U into rows.
228	    return [[columns[col][row] for col in range(dim)] for row in range(dim)]

231	def measurement_probabilities(program: Program, basis_probabilities: list[float]) -> dict[str, float]:
232	    """Aggregate basis-state probabilities into classical-outcome probabilities.
233	
234	    Uses the same qubit-to-clbit mapping as :func:`sample_counts` (each
235	    measured qubit contributes its bit to the classical index; unwritten
236	    clbits stay 0) and the same fixed-width, lexicographically ordered key
237	    convention. With no measurements the only possible outcome is the
238	    all-zero string, carrying total probability 1.
239	    """
240	    width = program.num_clbits
241	    measurements = [(op.targets[0], op.targets[1]) for op in program.operations if op.kind == "measure"]
242	
243	    if not measurements:
244	        return {format(0, f"0{width}b") if width else "": 1.0}
245	
246	    aggregated: dict[int, float] = {}
247	    for basis, probability in enumerate(basis_probabilities):
248	        classical = 0
249	        for qubit, clbit in measurements:
250	            if (basis >> qubit) & 1:
251	                classical |= 1 << clbit
252	        aggregated[classical] = aggregated.get(classical, 0.0) + probability
253	
254	    return {
255	        format(classical, f"0{width}b") if width else "": probability
256	        for classical, probability in sorted(aggregated.items())
257	    }

260	def sample_counts(program: Program, state: list[complex], shots: int, seed: int) -> dict[str, int]:
261	    """Draw *shots* samples from *state* deterministically from *seed*.
262	
263	    Returns a mapping from fixed-width classical bit strings (highest clbit
264	    index first) to occurrence counts. Only observed outcomes are present.
265	    """
266	    probabilities = [abs(amplitude) ** 2 for amplitude in state]
267	    return sample_counts_from_probabilities(program, probabilities, shots, seed)

269	
270	def sample_counts_from_probabilities(
271	    program: Program, probabilities: list[float], shots: int, seed: int
272	) -> dict[str, int]:
273	    """Draw *shots* samples from explicit basis-state probabilities.
274	
275	    Used by the density-matrix path, which supplies the diagonal of the
276	    final density matrix; sampling semantics match the state-vector path.
277	    """
278	    measurements = [(op.targets[0], op.targets[1]) for op in program.operations if op.kind == "measure"]
279	
280	    total = sum(probabilities)
281	    cumulative = []
282	    running = 0.0
283	    for probability in probabilities:
284	        running += probability / total
285	        cumulative.append(running)
286	    if cumulative:
287	        cumulative[-1] = 1.0
288	
289	    rng = random.Random(seed)
290	    width = program.num_clbits
291	    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
292	    for _ in range(shots):
293	        point = rng.random()
294	        # Binary search for the first cumulative value >= point.
295	        lo, hi = 0, len(cumulative)
296	        while lo < hi:
297	            mid = (lo + hi) // 2
298	            if cumulative[mid] < point:
299	                lo = mid + 1
300	            else:
301	                hi = mid
302	        basis = lo
303	
304	        classical = 0
305	        for qubit, clbit in measurements:
306	            if (basis >> qubit) & 1:
307	                classical |= 1 << clbit
308	        key = format(classical, f"0{width}b") if width else ""
309	        counts[key] = counts.get(key, 0) + 1
310	
311	    return dict(sorted(counts.items()))

"""Result delivery: standard streams and atomic file export.

This is the only layer that writes standard output/error or result files.
Preparation and pure computation hand it either a ready success payload
(plus the command's exit code) or a
:class:`~quantum_circuit.errors.CommandFailure`; :class:`RunContext`
additionally implements the ``--output`` conflict protection, refusing to
export over any registered input before the command computes or re-runs
anything.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import stat
import sys
import tempfile

from .errors import CommandFailure


class RunContext:
    """Track the optional ``--output PATH`` target and every input file read.

    The target is absolutized once (anchored at the invocation working
    directory). Every non-stdin input the command reads is registered using
    the same path resolution used to open it. Conflicts are decided by real
    file identity (:func:`os.path.samefile` -- which follows symlinks,
    Windows junctions and hard links and folds case on case-insensitive
    volumes), not by comparing path strings, so relative ``.``/``..``
    aliases, different absolute spellings, links or case-only aliases cannot
    be used to export over a reproducibility input.

    A manifest-declared task path that currently does not exist (or is not
    readable) cannot be compared by identity; such an entry is registered
    with the same lexical path the preparation layer would open and
    compared lexically against the target when one side is absent.
    """

    def __init__(self, output: str | None):
        self.output_arg = output
        self.target: str | None = None if output is None else os.path.abspath(output)
        # Absolute, lexically normalized spellings of every protected input.
        self.inputs: set[str] = set()

    def register_input(self, path: str, base_dir: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Register *path* as an input the command actually read."""
        if self.target is None or path == "-":
            return
        self.inputs.add(_absolute_input(path, base_dir))

    def register_declared(self, path: str, base_dir: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Register a path a validated manifest declares as a task input.

        The file need not exist or be readable. When it happens to exist
        (possibly through a symlinked manifest directory), conflict
        detection still compares it by identity; a genuinely absent
        declaration falls back to lexical comparison.
        """
        if self.target is None or path == "-":
            return
        self.inputs.add(_absolute_input(path, base_dir))

    def is_conflict(self, input_path: str) -> bool:
        """Return whether *input_path* names the same file as the target."""
        target = self.target
        assert target is not None
        # Whenever both sides exist, real file identity settles it:
        # os.path.samefile follows symlinks and Windows junctions, joins
        # hard links through (st_dev, st_ino), and reports equal identity
        # for case-only aliases on volumes that fold case.
        if os.path.exists(target) and os.path.exists(input_path):
            try:
                return os.path.samefile(target, input_path)
            except OSError:
                pass
        # At least one side does not exist (the normal case for a declared
        # but missing task) or identity could not be computed: fall back to
        # the lexical view of both absolute spellings, folding letter case
        # only on volumes that actually do so.
        return _lexically_same_file(target, input_path)


def _absolute_input(path: str, base_dir: str | None) -> str:
    """Absolutize an input path exactly the way the command opens it."""
    if base_dir is not None and not os.path.isabs(path):
        path = os.path.join(base_dir, path)
    return os.path.abspath(path)


# Case-folding probe results, cached per probed existing directory.
_case_folding_dirs: dict[str, bool] = {}


def _probe_case_folding(directory: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether *directory* (an existing dir) folds letter case.

    Detected read-only whenever the directory has at least one entry whose
    name carries a letter case: the entry and its case-swapped spelling are
    compared; equal identity means the volume folds case (distinct entries
    can only coexist on a case-sensitive volume). An empty or unlistable
    directory falls back to a create-and-remove probe, and failure to create
    one (a read-only directory) to the platform convention.
    """
    cached = _case_folding_dirs.get(directory)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached

    folding = _case_folding_from_entries(directory)
    if folding is None:
        folding = _case_folding_from_probe(directory)
    _case_folding_dirs[directory] = folding
    return folding


def _case_folding_from_entries(directory: str) -> bool | None:
    """Read-only case-folding test using the directory's own entries."""
    try:
        entries = os.listdir(directory)
    except OSError:
        return None
    for name in entries:
        swapped = name.swapcase()
        if swapped == name:
            continue
        direct = os.path.join(directory, name)
        folded = os.path.join(directory, swapped)
        try:
            return os.path.samefile(direct, folded)
        except OSError:
            # The swapped spelling does not resolve (case-sensitive volume)
            # or neither entry can be stated; move on to the next entry.
            continue
    return None


def _case_folding_from_probe(directory: str) -> bool:
    """Create-and-remove probe for directories without cased entries."""
    probe: str | None = None
    try:
        try:
            fd, probe = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".qcs-caseprobe-", dir=directory)
        except OSError:
            return os.name == "nt" or sys.platform == "darwin"
        os.close(fd)
        name = os.path.basename(probe)
        return os.path.exists(os.path.join(directory, name.swapcase()))
    finally:
        if probe is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(probe)
            except OSError:
                pass


def _path_case_folding(path: str) -> bool:
    """Return whether the volume hosting *path* folds letter case.

    The file itself need not exist; the nearest existing ancestor directory
    is probed, since case sensitivity is a directory/volume property.
    """
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.normpath(path)) or "."
    while not os.path.isdir(directory):
        parent = os.path.dirname(directory)
        if parent == directory:
            # No existing ancestor (e.g. an unmapped Windows drive): fall
            # back to the platform convention.
            return os.name == "nt" or sys.platform == "darwin"
        directory = parent
    return _probe_case_folding(directory)


def _lexically_same_file(left: str, right: str) -> bool:
    """Compare two absolute spellings without relying on either file existing.

    ``.``/``..`` segments are normalized away first. Letter case is folded
    only when both paths live on case-folding volumes; on a case-sensitive
    volume two case-only spellings are genuinely different files.
    """
    left = os.path.normpath(left)
    right = os.path.normpath(right)
    if left == right:
        return True
    if _path_case_folding(left) and _path_case_folding(right):
        return left.lower() == right.lower()
    return False


def register_manifest_references(
    ctx: RunContext,
    jobs: list[dict[str, object]],
    base_dir: str | None,
) -> None:
    """Register every circuit/noise path a *validated* manifest names.

    Conflict protection is based on the manifest's declared references,
    not only on files that opened successfully, so a failed task cannot
    export a report over a path a later re-run would treat as input. The
    manifest is structurally valid at this point (paths are non-``-``
    strings); a missing or unreadable file is still covered, compared
    lexically against the output target using the manifest directory base.
    Comparison itself is decided per entry later: an existing file by
    identity, an absent declaration lexically.
    """
    if ctx.target is None:
        return
    for job in jobs:
        source = str(job["source"])
        ctx.register_declared(source, base_dir)
        noise_model = job.get("noise_model")
        if noise_model is not None:
            ctx.register_declared(str(noise_model), base_dir)


def output_conflict(ctx: RunContext) -> CommandFailure | None:
    """Refuse to export over an input file (``output_error``, exit code 2).

    Existing inputs and target are compared by real file identity, so
    relative ``.``/``..`` aliases, different absolute spellings, symbolic
    links, Windows junctions or hard links -- and case-only aliases on
    case-folding volumes -- all conflict; two genuinely different files
    never do. A manifest-declared input that is currently missing or
    unreadable is compared by lexical normalization instead.

    Invoked only after the command's own validation has succeeded but
    before any result-producing computation runs, so no simulation or
    re-run task executes and no file is modified.
    """
    if ctx.target is None:
        return None
    for input_path in ctx.inputs:
        if ctx.is_conflict(input_path):
            return CommandFailure(
                "output_error",
                f"output path {ctx.output_arg!r} is the same file as an input read by this command",
                2,
            )
    return None


def emit_failure(failure: CommandFailure) -> None:
    """Write one failure as the canonical single-line stderr JSON."""
    sys.stderr.write(json.dumps(failure.to_payload()) + "\n")


def write_output_atomic(target: str, data: bytes) -> str | None:
    """Write *data* to *target* without ever leaving a partial result.

    Returns ``None`` on success, otherwise a human-readable error message.
    The data lands in a temporary file in the target's parent directory and
    is moved into place atomically, so a failure leaves any pre-existing
    target byte-for-byte unchanged and removes the temporary file.
    """

    if not os.path.isdir(parent):
        return f"cannot write output {target!r}: parent directory does not exist"

    # followed (a link to a regular file is a valid target; os.replace swaps
    # the link itself without touching its referent), while a directory --
    # including a symlink to one -- and other non-regular types are refused.

    except OSError as exc:

        kind = "a directory" if stat.S_ISDIR(existing.st_mode) else "not a regular file"
        return f"cannot write output {target!r}: target is {kind}"

                else 0o666 & ~current_umask
            )
            os.fchmod(fd, mode)
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                handle.write(data)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        except OSError as exc:
            return f"cannot write output {target!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}"
        try:
            os.replace(tmp_name, target)
        except OSError as exc:
            return f"cannot write output {target!r}: {exc.strerror or exc}"
        tmp_name = None
    finally:
        if tmp_name is not None:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp_name)
            except OSError:
                pass
    return None


def finish(ctx: RunContext | None, result: dict[str, object], exit_code: int) -> int:
    """Emit a ready result: stdout as before, or the exported file.

    With no ``--output`` the stdout/stderr/exit behavior is exactly the
    historical one. With an export, stdout stays empty and the original
    exit code (including the batch/reconcile code 3) is preserved whenever
    the file lands; an export failure is an ``output_error`` with code 1.
    """
    if ctx is None or ctx.target is None:
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(result) + "\n")
        return exit_code
    if ctx.output_arg == "-":
        emit_failure(CommandFailure("output_error", "output path must not be '-'", 1))
        return 1
    message = write_output_atomic(ctx.target, (json.dumps(result) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
    if message is not None:
        emit_failure(CommandFailure("output_error", message, 1))
        return 1
    return exit_code
